subject: Pilot packaging options: compact pilot -> throughput-dedicated path
messages:
From: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really helpful. We ran the pilot on the Compact tier for two weeks and saw a sharp spike in week 2. Before we run a larger pilot we want clarity on the upgrade/downgrade mechanics and how feature bundles map across tiers. Specific questions: 

- If we upgrade mid-quarter from Compact (trial) to a High-Throughput Dedicated pool, how is proration handled?
- Do feature entitlements (batching priority, KV cache persist, binary embeddings) move with the tier or remain add-ons?
- If demand subsides, what downgrade path exists and are there credits for unused committed throughput?

Attached is a small usage snapshot from the pilot (opsly_usage_snapshot.csv) — we can walk through it if helpful.

Can you propose a few upgrade scenarios with cost delta and any short-term credits you can offer?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Redding
Head of Platform
Opsly

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Hi Tom — great to hear the pilot surface load. I pulled together a short comparison for Compact vs High-Throughput and three upgrade scenarios (attached: redwood_plan_comparison.pdf). Quick answers up front:

- Proration: upgrades are pro-rated to the day. If you move mid-billing-cycle we'll charge the delta for the remaining days and apply any promotional credits agreed at contract sign.
- Feature entitlements: we classify a set of "Enterprise features" (dedicated KV persistence, priority batching, sustained burst slots). Those are tied to the tier unless explicitly purchased as add-ons — meaning an upgrade will enable them automatically; downgrades will remove entitlement unless you keep them as add-ons.
- Downgrade credits: we typically do not credit past usage, but we offer a one-time migration buffer for first-year upgrades (see doc). For downgrades we provide a 30-day fallback policy: you can move back to hosted with preserved model versioning, but committed-capacity refunds are limited to negotiated concessions.

Next steps: 1) Share a 30-day hourly token/throughput slice (if you can export from the pilot), 2) pick one of the three scenarios in the PDF and we’ll run a pro-forma.

I copied Lauren to confirm we can extend a short migration buffer if Opsly signs a 12-month reserved commitment.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Tom / team — quick follow-up from pricing:

Option A (short pilot burst): 2-week Dedicated burst with no long-term commit — includes 100k token burst credits and access to priority batching. Price: $7,500 for the burst (one-time).

Option B (12-month reserve): Yearly reserved High-Throughput pool. Standard list delta vs Compact is ~3.2x for throughput units. We can extend a 10% first-year discount on committed spend, or 15% if you sign within 10 business days.

Migration credit proposal: For first-year upgrades we will apply a one-time credit equal to two weeks of your expected committed throughput ($ estimate in attached opsly_pricing_draft.xlsx). Downgrades: we can allow step-downs at quarter boundaries with a 60-day notice, but refunds on unused committed capacity are limited to 25% of remaining quarter credits unless we negotiate a larger concession at contract execution.

Happy to run numbers against the CSV you sent — Ben

From: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from Opsly procurement and platform: 

- The 25% cap on unused committed credits for step-downs feels risky for us. If we commit to a year and traffic drops abruptly, Opsly needs a clearer rollback with predictable economics. Is there a middle ground (e.g., credit smoothing over two quarters)?
- If we keep models pinned but fall back to hosted on lower load, will KV cache persistence (an enterprise feature) lose warm cache state? If so, that would impact latency for certain flows.

We'd like a brief call (30m) to iron this out. Karen and I are available Thurs 9/2 AM PT.

—Tom

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Tom — appreciate the candor. Two pragmatic options to propose (aimed at lowering Opsly's downgrade risk):

1) Smoothing credit: instead of a single 25% cap, we can offer a graduated smoothing refund: 50% of unused committed credits reimbursed in the first quarter after step-down, 25% in the second quarter. This is tied to a clear rollback window and usage thresholds.

2) Hybrid fallback: keep model/pinning and a lightweight KV snapshot service for 30 days on fallback to hosted. This preserves warm-state for critical endpoints but at a lower persistence SLA. It would be a low-cost add-on and avoids full cold-starts.

Operational asks from our side: export of hourly token volumes (Hannah requested) and a short list of critical endpoints where warm cache matters. Priyom can model the cost delta if you share the list.

If that sounds reasonable we can put the smoothing language and KV snapshot add-on into the MSA as an amendment.

-Lauren
VP, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Redding <tom.redding@opsly.com>, Karen Li <karen.li@opsly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: compact -> high-throughput path?

Tom / Karen — thanks all. Quick summary and proposed MAP: 

1) Opsly shares the hourly token dump + 3 endpoints that need warm KV persistence by EOD 9/2.
2) Redwood runs pro-forma for Option B (12-month reserve) with the smoothing-credit language and a priced KV snapshot add-on — deliver by 9/6.
3) If Opsly signs within 10 business days we hold the 15% first-year commit discount and apply the two-week migration credit at execution.
4) Schedule: 30m call Thurs 9/2 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent).

Link to draft e-sign (for timeline/terms only, not final MSA): https://www.docusign.com/sign/opsly-redwood-commit-v1

Ben / Priyom / I will join the call. Tom — I’ll send the calendar invite and a short checklist for the hourly export.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
